_comment: temper-constraint-compiler's expected-failure manifest, the sibling of
wasm_expected_failures.json (temper-drc-rs), wasm_expected_failures_geometry.json,
wasm_expected_failures_thermal.json, wasm_expected_failures_router_core.json and
wasm_expected_failures_design_bundle.json. Same contract -- see
wasm_expected_failures.json's _comment for why divergences are LISTED and executed
rather than deleted or cfg'd out.
This one is EMPTY, and that is a result rather than an omission: measured 2026-08-10,
70 tests are registered, 69 of them exist on wasm32, and all 69 pass.
THE 70th IS NOT AN EXCLUSION MADE HERE. constraints::tests::
host_libm_symbols_actually_resolve carries its own
`#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]` in constraints/mod.rs, written by the crate
long before this registry existed: it asserts that dlsym() resolves the host libm's
`pow`, and wasm32-unknown-unknown has no dynamic loader, so the function does not
exist on this target. gen_wasm_test_registry.py copies that cfg onto the registry
entry (see fn_cfgs()), so the test is absent rather than failing -- the same
`no-dynamic-loader` fact temper-drc-rs records as an expected failure, but reached
one step earlier, at compile time. It is counted in the PR's arithmetic as
'registered 70, executable 69'.
The file still exists because run_wasm_tests.mjs defaults to the temper-drc-rs
manifest, and pointing a constraint-compiler-only module at THAT one would report
every drc entry as an orphan exclusion and exit non-zero. `make
wasm-constraint-compiler-test` passes this file.
An empty manifest is NOT a weaker gate: with nothing excluded, all 69 executable
tests are load-bearing and any regression on wasm32 turns the step red.
